title: Sequence recovery checkpoint is stored at a hardcoded shared path, so a brand-new profile was offered another database's interrupted run -- and discarding it deleted that run's recovery data
what_happened: On a --fresh profile whose database contains zero rows in sequences, sequence_runs and sequence_checkpoints, the app popped a modal 'Recover Sequence? A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed. Sequence: AUDIT SEQ, Saved 0m ago, Completed 16 frames (0m integration)' -- on top of the First Night Walkthrough of a first-run user. The checkpoint is written to ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint, ignoring SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR/SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR, and belongs to a different data directory entirely (its save_path is /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-run/captures). The modal has only Discard/Resume and Escape does not dismiss it, so to continue I had to press Discard -- which deleted both the checkpoint and its .bak, destroying the other instance's recovery state. Two further problems in the same file: the checkpoint says executor_state='Completed' and is_active=false while the dialog calls it 'interrupted'; and completed_exposures=16 with completed_integration_secs=0.0 for a 3.0 s x 20 node, which the UI renders as '16 frames (0m integration)'.
expected: The recovery checkpoint must live under the active data directory so it can never describe a run that is not in the open database, the dialog must not offer to resume a run whose executor_state is Completed, and a fresh install must never see this modal.
repro: 1. Run instance A against data dir X, start and interrupt a sequence named AUDIT SEQ. 2. Start instance B with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=Y (empty DB). 3. B shows 'Recover Sequence? ... AUDIT SEQ'. 4. sqlite3 Y/skotiq.db 'select * from sequence_checkpoints' -> empty. 5. Press Discard in B -> ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint and .bak are both gone.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-32-firstnight.png (the modal on a fresh profile), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/checkpoint-evidence.json (the checkpoint: name 'AUDIT SEQ', save_path /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-run/captures, executor_state 'Completed', is_active false, completed_exposures 16, completed_integration_secs 0.0); my DB's sequences/sequence_runs/sequence_checkpoints all returned zero rows
where: native checkpoint writer -> ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint (path resolution ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR); recovery prompt raised from app_shell
proposed_fix: Resolve the checkpoint path from the same data-dir resolver the database uses, stamp the owning database/profile id into the checkpoint and refuse to offer recovery when it does not match, and gate the prompt on executor_state != Completed.
verdict_reasoning: Core mechanism independently reproduced LIVE, by accident, mid-verification. My equipment-shell-verify instance (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/equipment-shell-verify/data, whose DB returned 0 rows from sequences, sequence_runs AND sequence_checkpoints) was shown 'Recover Sequence? A previous sequence was interrupted... Sequence: New Sequence' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-46-flerror2.png). The checkpoint at ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint had save_path /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes/captures -- a concurrently running agent's data dir. Escape did not dismiss it (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-47-esc.png). Relaunching with XDG_DATA_HOME redirected into my scratch dir made the prompt vanish, proving the path is XDG/getApplicationSupportDirectory-derived (app_shell.dart:347-348) and ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR, which the rest of native persistence does honour (e.g. calibration_handlers.dart:110). Discard is destructive as claimed: CheckpointManager::clear() (native/.../sequencer/src/checkpoint.rs:746-757) removes both the primary and the .bak. HOWEVER one sub-claim is REFUTED: the dialog cannot have been raised from a checkpoint whose executor_state is 'Completed' and is_active false. can_resume() (checkpoint.rs:481-492) requires is_active && state in {Running, Paused}, and app_shell returns noRecovery when !canResume. My live capture showed executor_state=Paused, is_active=true. The reporter's checkpoint-evidence.json is a LATER snapshot -- mark_completed() (checkpoint.rs:765-771) rewrites exactly those two fields when the other instance's run finished. Severity P1 -> P2: on a real single install there is one support dir and one DB, so cross-database contamination requires an explicit SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR override; the genuine defect is the resolver disagreeing with the rest of native persistence plus a cross-instance-destructive Discard.

title: Equipment readiness panel omits the mount entirely when it is disconnected
what_happened: With all four profile devices (camera, mount, focuser, filter wheel) disconnected, the STATUS panel listed only two device items: 'Critical devices - Camera is not connected' and 'Profile devices - Assigned in your profile but not connected: Focuser, Filter Wheel. They will be unavailable this session.' The mount is not mentioned in either item, or anywhere else on the screen. A user scanning the readiness list before heading out would conclude the mount is fine.
expected: Every profile device that is not connected must appear in the readiness list, and a disconnected mount should be a blocking/critical item -- it is the one failure that ends a night outright.
repro: 1. Profile with camera, mount, focuser and filter wheel assigned. 2. Equipment > Disconnect All. 3. Read the STATUS panel: only Camera (critical) and 'Focuser, Filter Wheel' (profile devices) are listed.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-readiness-mount.png, full context /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-80-coolonconnect.png (main area reads 'No devices connected', pill 0/4)
proposed_fix: Build the 'Profile devices' list from every assigned-but-unconnected device including the mount, and promote mount to the critical tier alongside camera.
verdict_reasoning: Behaviour reproduced: with all four profile devices disconnected I opened the full 'Ready to image' dialog (View all) and it lists exactly two device items -- 'Critical devices: Camera is not connected' and 'Profile devices: Assigned in your profile but not connected: Focuser, Filter Wheel' -- with the mount named nowhere (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-10-viewall.png). Cause: readiness_provider.dart:105-112 deliberately filters camera and mount OUT of offlineProfileDevices ('already covered by the critical-devices item'), while _buildCriticalDevices (readiness_models.dart:310-357) reports only the single highest-priority fault, so the mount branch is masked whenever the camera is also down. Two parts of the finding are overstated: the mount IS already in the critical tier (it surfaces as 'Mount is not connected - you can capture but cannot slew or track' the instant the camera connects, so 'promote mount to the critical tier' is a no-op), and it is not absent 'anywhere else on the screen' -- the profile card shows 0/4 with per-device dots and the status bar reads 'Mount Disconnected'. Severity P1 -> P2.

title: Red night theme renders full-saturation blue, cyan and green accent swatches
what_happened: Settings > Appearance > Theme > 'Red night' correctly re-tints the whole shell, nav rail, cards and status bar in red. The 'Accent color' swatch row directly underneath it, however, stays fully saturated. Sampling the rendered pixels: (91,158,196) blue, (16,185,129) green, (245,158,11) amber, (239,68,68) red, (40,120,168) blue, (236,72,153) pink, (6,182,212) cyan. Cyan and green at those levels are exactly the short-wavelength, high-luminance content red-night mode exists to eliminate.
expected: In red night mode every pixel should be red-channel-dominant. Either desaturate the accent swatches to red-luminance stand-ins (with the name as the differentiator) or hide the accent picker in red night with a note that accent colour does not apply.
repro: 1. Settings > Appearance > Theme = Red night. 2. Look at the Accent color row on the same page. 3. Sample the swatch pixels.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-62-rednight.png (whole page red, swatches not), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-dd3.png (close-up with the Red night dropdown open); pixel samples at y=443: x=1524 (91,158,196), x=1553 (16,185,129), x=1698 (6,182,212)
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/... appearance accent-colour row (swatches bypass the red-night colour filter)
proposed_fix: Route the accent swatches through the same red-night transform as the rest of the theme, or replace them with labelled red-tinted chips while red night is active.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and re-measured independently at full resolution. With Theme = Red night the whole shell is red (sampled surfaces: nav rail (0,0,0), card (20,8,8)) but the Accent color row is untouched: (91,158,196), (16,185,129), (245,158,11), (239,68,68), (40,120,168), (236,72,153), (6,182,212) -- the exact values the reporter cited. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-30-rednight.png and eqv-29-rednight-raw.png. The green and cyan are precisely the short-wavelength high-luminance content red-night mode exists to remove. Severity P2 stands.

title: Window minimize / maximize / close disappear below ~800px window width, leaving no way to close the app
what_happened: The desktop build draws its own title bar (no OS decorations). At 1600x900 and at 900x750 the bar carries remote-status, notifications, account, settings, minimize, maximize and close. Resizing the window to 760x700 switches the shell to the mobile layout (bottom navigation bar: Home/Gear/Imaging/Sequence/Guiding/Plan/More) and the title bar collapses to just the wordmark and a single settings gear -- minimize, maximize and close are gone, along with the notifications and account buttons. With no OS decorations there is then no mouse-reachable way to close or minimize the window.
expected: Window controls belong to the desktop window regardless of width; the responsive breakpoint should never strip them. If the mobile shell is deliberately reused below the breakpoint, it must still render the platform window controls on desktop.
repro: 1. Launch the Linux desktop build. 2. Resize the window to 760x700 (xdotool windowsize <win> 760 700). 3. Inspect the top bar: only the SKOTIQ wordmark and a gear remain.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-vnarrow-title.png (760px title bar), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-narrow.png (900px title bar with all controls), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-vnarrow.png (bottom nav bar appears)
proposed_fix: Keep the desktop title-bar window controls in every layout on desktop platforms; gate only the label density on width.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced: xdotool windowsize 760 700 on the Linux release bundle switched the shell to the mobile layout (bottom nav Home/Gear/Imaging/Sequence/Guiding/Plan/More) and the title bar collapsed to the SKOTIQ wordmark plus a single settings gear -- minimize, maximize, close, notifications and account all gone (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-32-narrow-crop.png). That bar is _MobileSettingsBar (app_shell.dart:865-916), which renders no window controls at all. The finding's premise that there are no OS decorations to fall back on also holds on Linux: apps/desktop/lib/main.dart:161 sets titleBarStyle: TitleBarStyle.hidden and window_manager's Linux plugin implements that as gtk_window_set_decorated(false). Minor overstatement: Alt+F4 and WM keyboard/menu paths still close the window, and widening past the breakpoint restores the controls, so 'no way to close the app' should read 'no mouse-reachable window control'. Severity P2 stands.

title: The 'Deleted <profile>' snackbar never auto-dismisses and covers the entire status bar
what_happened: Deleting an equipment profile raises a full-width bottom snackbar 'Deleted "My First Rig"  [Undo]'. It was still on screen 7 minutes later (delete confirmed at 11:36:45, snackbar still present in the AT-SPI tree at 11:43:29), it survived navigating from Equipment to Settings to Dashboard, it has no close button, and clicking elsewhere does not dismiss it. While it is up, the whole status bar -- profile name, device connection states, focuser position, temperature, clock and LST -- is hidden. Only restarting the app cleared it.
expected: An undo snackbar should auto-dismiss after a few seconds (or on navigation), and should not permanently occlude the status bar.
repro: 1. Equipment > right-click a profile > Delete > Delete. 2. Snackbar appears over the status bar. 3. Navigate to Settings and then Dashboard, wait several minutes -- it is still there.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-95-share.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-96-snackbar.png (snackbar over the status bar on two different screens); AT-SPI tree at 11:43:29 still contains 'Deleted "My First Rig"' + Undo button, delete performed 11:36:45
proposed_fix: Give the snackbar a finite duration (e.g. 6 s), make it floating rather than full-width so it does not sit on the status bar, and add a dismiss affordance.
verdict_reasoning: Behaviour reproduced precisely -- deleted a profile at 12:28:32, the snackbar 'Deleted "My First Rig" [Undo]' was still on screen at 12:30:04 (92 s) after navigating Equipment -> Dashboard, covering the entire status bar with no close affordance (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-40-snackbar.png, eqv-43-snacklate.png). BUT the diagnosis and the proposed fix are wrong and would change nothing: equipment_screen.dart:439 ALREADY sets duration: const Duration(seconds: 6). The real cause is a Flutter 3.44 framework default -- SnackBar's constructor sets persist = persist ?? action != null (flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/material/snack_bar.dart:303), and ScaffoldMessengerState's timer callback returns early without hiding when snackBar.persist is true (scaffold.dart:618-622). So EVERY snackbar in this app that carries an action never times out, which makes this a systemic issue, not a profile-delete one. Correct fix is persist: false (or showCloseIcon), not a duration. Severity P2 stands but the scope is wider than reported.

title: Diagnostic dump is described as 'recent log files' but bundles 7 days of logs from every Skotiq instance on the machine
what_happened: Settings > Help & Tutorials > Generate Diagnostic Dump promises 'Recent log files -- logs/exported_logs.txt -- rotated native logs + in-app entries'. The produced zip contained a 4.78 MB, 38,299-line exported_logs.txt spanning 2026-07-26 through 2026-08-01, and 421 of its lines reference /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-run -- a completely different profile's capture directory, including that run's target names and FITS filenames. The native log is written to the hardcoded ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs/ regardless of SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR, so the dump is not scoped to the session or the data directory the user is running. The save dialog also defaults to the application's own bundle directory (apps/desktop/build/linux/x64/release/bundle), which in a real install is typically read-only.
expected: 'Recent log files' should mean the current session (or a bounded window), scoped to the running data directory; and the save dialog should default to a writable user location such as Downloads or the configured capture folder.
repro: 1. Settings > Help & Tutorials > Generate Diagnostic Dump > Open > Create dump. 2. Note the save dialog opens inside the app bundle directory. 3. Save and inspect: unzip -p dump.zip logs/exported_logs.txt | grep -c . -> 38299 lines, dates 2026-07-26..2026-08-01, and grep for other profiles' paths.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-72-dump.png (the 'Recent log files' claim), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-73-dump2.png (save dialog defaulting into the bundle dir), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/diagdump.zip and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/dumplog.txt (7 days, 421 lines referencing /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-run)
proposed_fix: Bound the log export to the current session or last N hours, resolve the log directory from the active data dir, state the actual span in the UI, and default the save location to the user's Downloads/capture folder.
verdict_reasoning: Every element verified. (a) The 'Recent log files / logs/exported_logs.txt' copy is at diagnostic_dump_screen.dart:194-195. (b) It is produced by LoggingService.exportLogs (logging_service.dart:378-410), which concatenates EVERY file returned by getLogFiles (336-365 -- all files in the log dir whose path contains 'skotiq.log') with no time bound whatsoever. (c) The log dir is getApplicationSupportDirectory()/logs (desktop_logging_init.dart:61-68), independent of SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR -- confirmed on disk: ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs holds 7 daily rotations 2026-07-26..2026-08-01 totalling 4.9 MB, and today's file was being written by MY scratch instance (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/equipment-shell-verify/data) while I ran it. (d) Cross-instance leakage measured directly: today's shared log contains 454 lines referencing three other audit profiles' capture directories (/tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-run, /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes, /tmp/ns-audit/equipment-shell). (e) The save-dialog claim holds: diagnostic_dump_screen.dart:132-140 calls chooseExportTarget with no initialDirectory and export_target.dart:74-78 passes that null straight to file_selector.getSaveLocation, so the picker opens at the process CWD. Severity P2 stands.
